SASRec scores candidates by dot product with a shared item-embedding table and already normalizes its final sequence representation ([original implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py)). Algebraically, an additional LayerNorm can change rankings: centering introduces candidate-dependent terms, while learned coordinate gains and biases change scoring geometry. Initializing gain=1 and bias=0 does not make LayerNorm an identity ([Layer Normalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.06450)). A common positive scalar applied only to candidate embeddings preserves rankings for fixed features, but changes loss temperature and training gradients. Scaling a tied embedding table also changes sequence inputs and the pooling branch, so ranking invariance no longer follows. Preserve baseline embedding scales and distinguish input scaling from output-logit scaling.

For function-preserving initialization, use h_new=h_baseline+α·r(recent_items), with α=0 and any new normalization confined inside r. This follows the zero-gated residual principle in [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887). Conversely, LN(h_baseline+αr) becomes LN(h_baseline) at zero gate. Use a zero-initialized scalar or tanh gate; sigmoid(0)=0.5. Keep the branch nonzero at initialization: simultaneously zeroing its output and gate can block both gradients.

Recommended ablations: unchanged baseline; normalization-only with gate fixed at zero; normalization plus learned residual; baseline plus learned residual without extra skip-path normalization. Match backbone initialization, data order, optimizer, training budget, and checkpoint selection; initialize new modules without shifting the backbone RNG stream. Verify initial logits against the corresponding control in evaluation mode. Compare pinned macro validation HR@10 and report branch/base norms and gate values. A shuffled-history or uniform-pooling control helps separate recency information from added capacity.
